say: Let's look at a ball kicked across a football pitch.

do.text: Why does a kicked ball curve?

say: The moment it leaves your foot, the ball is doing two things at once.
Forward, it keeps the same speed, because nothing pushes it back.
Upward, gravity pulls on it every second, so it rises, slows down, then falls.

do.text: Upward: $y = u sin(theta) t - (1/2) g t^2$

say: Put the two motions together and you get this curve. It is called a parabola.
At the very top, the ball is still moving forward. It has only stopped going up.
So the curve is just two simple motions happening together.
